headline: Self-trust is believing in your own judgment—the foundation for decisive action and authentic living
universal_truth: Confidence comes from evidence; trust yourself because you've earned it, not just hoped for it
fun_facts: Imposter syndrome affects an estimated 70% of people at some point in their lives
Self-trust isn't about being right—it's about handling being wrong
People who trust themselves paradoxically become more open to feedback, not less
discussion_questions: When do you trust yourself most?
What has damaged your self-trust in the past?
How do you rebuild trust in yourself after a failure?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Everyone faces moments of doubt: Can I do this? Am I qualified? What if I'm wrong? Self-trust isn't arrogance—it's the calm confidence that you can handle whatever happens, including failure. Without it, you second-guess every move.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Self-trust seems like something you either have or don't. But where does it actually come from? Is it just personality, or can it be built?

options.text: Self-trust is built through experience—keeping promises to yourself, surviving difficulties, and proving your capability through action
options.response: Yes. Self-trust comes from evidence, not affirmations. Each time you do what you said you'd do, each difficulty you survive, you accumulate proof that you're trustworthy.

options.text: Self-trust comes from positive thinking and believing in yourself
options.response: Positive thinking helps, but self-trust requires evidence—actions that prove your reliability...

q1.title: Promises to Yourself
q1.script: Every broken promise to yourself damages self-trust. Saying you'll exercise, then skipping it. Saying you'll finish, then quitting. Self-trust is built by keeping commitments to yourself. Start small. Prove you're reliable.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Promises to Yourself"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Surviving Difficulty
q2.script: You don't know what you can handle until you've handled it. Each challenge you survive expands your sense of capability. Difficulty isn't just something to avoid—it's where self-trust is forged.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Trust and Feedback
q3.script: Paradoxically, people with strong self-trust are more open to feedback, not less. They're secure enough to hear criticism without crumbling. Self-trust isn't thinking you're always right—it's knowing you can handle being wrong.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Confidence comes from evidence. Trust yourself because you've earned it through actions, not just hoped for it. Build proof, one kept promise at a time.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 191. Tomorrow, we'll explore knowing who you are—identity. Until then, make one small promise to yourself and keep it.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Small Promise - Build Evidence
growTrack.activity: Make one small, specific promise to yourself today and keep it. Not a big goal—something achievable. Do what you said you'd do. Notice how it feels. Self-trust is built one kept promise at a time.
